analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials TGIF ... 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: Global markets sold off overnight into 11/6: KOSPI and Nikkei each down about 6% (the note writes '~600bps'), Europe down 1.5-2%. US stocks were up modestly at the open, led by technology. German industrial production beat expectations.
Crude paused after Qatar's Emir spoke with the US President about de-escalating the Iran war. Corn is down to $4.40, and the desk calls the retreat in crop prices notable.
10-year yield at 4.85%, dollar bouncing, Bitcoin at $76k after a sharp move lower the prior day. Nonfarm payrolls consensus is 70k, and University of Michigan sentiment is also due.

Privo on risk: de-grossing remains acute. Nasdaq has broken its 200-day moving average and the S&P sits just above it, which needs to hold. Negative gamma leaves scope for violent moves in either direction.

Privo sees the de-rating as justified by fundamental uncertainty, but the last leg looks overextended in assets where forced de-risking has entrenched. Names cited: higher-quality tech such as TSMC and ASML.
Privo says the narrative changes on political reflexivity around AI investment and growth, stabilization in funding markets, and evidence that spending and demand remain intact.

Privo stands by the pre-election view: the S&P has been higher 12 months after every one of the 19 midterms since 1950. He calls this a 12-month observation, not a one-month forecast, and expects defensive positioning into the weekend.

GS Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10, back in the panic zone (9.5+). The roughly 5-point jump was the 3rd largest daily rise ever, after Wednesday's drop that was the 4th largest ever. The combined two-day swing is the largest on record.

GIR (Adam Bubes) on the US data center construction cycle: hyperscaler capex now exceeds cash flow from operations, and the midterm results add potential constraints on development. The pipeline is split into under construction, high probability announcements (per Aterio) and medium/low probability announcements.

GIR sees good visibility into US data center construction spending growth through 2028. Projects under construction support strong growth through 2027 and just over half of the 2028 spending forecast. Visibility is limited beyond 2028, and GIR does not underwrite the 2029-2030 trajectory.
GIR says the midterm results could extend the duration of the data center cycle rather than significantly cut the total addressable market.
FLR Q3 missed on EPS and revenue. Awards were $10.9bn, backlog $34bn (+21%), and full-year EBITDA guidance of $500-525mm was reaffirmed.
TILE beat on EPS and EBITDA but missed on revenue, and lowered full-year revenue guidance while affirming earnings guidance.
AXON missed on EPS and revenue but beat on EBITDA. Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance are well below consensus. The earnings call is at 5pm with a 13% implied move.
JHX Q3 revenue and EBITDA guidance are below consensus, and the call is at 5pm with a 2% implied move.
KRMN beat on EPS and revenue and raised full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance. The call is at 4:30pm with a 13% implied move.
KTOS beat on EPS and adjusted EBITDA, with revenue in line. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance is below consensus at the midpoint, and FY27 EBITDA and revenue guidance are below consensus.
LASR beat strongly on EPS, revenue and EBITDA and guided Q4 revenue and EBITDA well above consensus. The call is at 5pm with a 17% implied move.
SARO was in line on revenue and EPS and raised full-year EBITDA, revenue and EPS guidance.
WSC beat slightly on EPS and EBITDA, beat on revenue, and raised full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance. The call is at 5:30pm with a 4% implied move.
earnings_insights: FLR Q3 EPS $0.77 reported vs $0.80 consensus est, revenue $3.72bn vs $4.2bn consensus est, EBITDA $142mm vs $145mm consensus est. New awards $10.9bn, book-to-burn 2.9x, backlog $34bn up 21%. Full-year EBITDA $500-525mm reaffirmed.

TILE Q3 EPS $0.68 vs $0.61 consensus est, revenue $367mm vs $378mm consensus est, EBITDA $69mm vs $64mm consensus est. Full-year revenue guidance lowered to $1.44-1.46bn from $1.46-1.49bn, earnings guidance affirmed.

AXON Q3 EPS $1.72 vs $1.89 consensus est, revenue $909mm vs $934mm consensus est, EBITDA $236mm vs $227mm consensus est. Q4 revenue guide below $990mm-1.01bn vs $1.07bn consensus est, Q4 EBITDA $245-250mm vs $275mm consensus est. Call at 5pm, 13% implied move.

JHX Q2 EBITDA $455mm, EPS $0.42 vs $0.42 consensus est. Q3 guidance revenue $1.06-1.14bn vs $1.13bn consensus est, EBITDA $298-320mm vs $340mm consensus est. Full year sales $4.99-5.133bn, EBITDA $1.446-1.534bn. Discontinued operations add noise. Call at 5pm, 2% implied move.

KRMN Q3 EPS $0.19 vs $0.15 consensus est, revenue $202mm vs $195mm consensus est. Full-year revenue guide $755-760mm vs $730-745mm prior, EBITDA $225-227mm vs $215-223mm prior. Call at 4:30pm, 13% implied move.

KTOS Q3 adjusted EBITDA $46.3mn vs $44.1mn consensus est, EPS $0.24 vs $0.21 consensus est, revenue $471.8mn in line, consolidated book-to-bill 2.2x. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guide $48-52mn, below consensus at the midpoint, Q4 revenue guide $480-510mn in line. FY27 adjusted EBITDA guide $230-240mn vs $241.5mn consensus est, revenue $2.10-2.20bn vs $2.22bn consensus est. Call at 5pm.

LASR Q3 EPS $0.16 vs $0.05 consensus est, revenue $74mm vs $68mm consensus est, EBITDA $11mm vs $5mm consensus est. Q4 guide revenue $84-90mm vs $75mm consensus est, EBITDA $12-18mm vs $8mm consensus est. Call at 5pm, 17% implied move.

SARO Q3 revenue $1.56bn in line, EPS in line, EBITDA $225mm (the note's consensus figure reads '$2221mm', apparently a typo). Full-year EBITDA $905-920mm vs $885-910mm prior, revenue $6.53-6.65bn vs $6.38-6.5bn prior, EPS $1.57-1.62 vs $1.5-1.57 prior. Call at 5pm, 5% implied move.

WSC Q3 EPS $0.29 vs $0.28 consensus est, EBITDA $234mm vs $233mm consensus est, revenue $601mm vs $586mm consensus est. Full-year revenue guide $2.34bn vs $2.18bn prior, EBITDA $920mm vs $900mm prior. Call at 5:30pm, 4% implied move.
